solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Member in B&B requires something for toast and fruit loaf

indicators.note: the limb is placed in between the two letters of the B&B abbreviation

parts.note: B&B, bed and breakfast, supplies two Bs
an arm is a member, a limb of the body
a toast rack holds slices of toast

explanation.surface: A guest house menu: something to put toast in, plus a fruit loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: BARMBRACK is an Irish speckled fruit bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A barmbrack is a traditional Irish yeasted bread studded with dried fruit, a kind of fruit loaf.

clue.text: Poisonous gas coming from a resin when crushed

indicators.note: crushing breaks up the words a resin so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toxic vapour released when a resin is pulverised.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsine is a highly toxic compound of arsenic and hydrogen that exists as a gas.

clue.text: End up more than once in a hut down under

indicators.note: the reversed piece is written twice over, more than once
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Someone finishing up repeatedly in an Australian shack.
explanation.definitionFit: A mia-mia is an Aboriginal shelter or temporary hut in Australia, the land down under.

clue.text: Harangue not initially helping

indicators.note: the first letter of the synonym is dropped, so it is no longer there initially

parts.note: a harangue is a long pompous speech, an oration

explanation.surface: A lecture that was no help at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like part of the surface but is the noun: a portion of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A helping is a portion or allowance of food, just as a ration is a fixed share.

clue.text: Regains consciousness from coma, not half sad

indicators.note: only half of the word coma is kept, the first two letters

parts.note: mesto is the Italian musical direction meaning sad or mournful

explanation.surface: A patient waking from a coma, still a little gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: MESTO is a musical term from Italian for 'sad', which a solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to is an idiom for recovering awareness after fainting or being knocked out.

clue.text: Romantic poet and old king on mountain top?

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a ridge is the crest or top line of a mountain

explanation.surface: A poet and an ancient ruler perched on a summit.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a nursery-rhyme king, 'a merry old soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Taylor Coleridge was one of the leading English poets of the Romantic movement.

clue.text: Account of previous events supports politician

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a Tory is a member of the British Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A history of what went before that endorses a Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstory is the history behind a character or situation, the events that came earlier.

clue.text: Certain to have finished under a legal obligation

parts.note: bound to happen means certain
when a thing is over it is finished

explanation.surface: Sure to be done with, yet still legally bound.
explanation.walkthrough: In British law a court may bind a person over to keep the peace.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bound over has been placed by a court under a formal duty, such as keeping the peace.

clue.text: To get a duck somewhere on WI tour?

parts.note: to bag something is to get or capture it
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A batsman scoring nothing somewhere on a West Indies cricket tour.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is West Indies; a duck is a cricket score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, a place a West Indies cricket tour could visit.

clue.text: Sweetener? As what you'd expect — insipid

parts.note: par is the normal or expected standard
tame means dull or insipid

explanation.surface: An artificial sweetener, predictably tasteless.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspartame is an artificial low-calorie sugar substitute used in diet drinks.

clue.text: Useless person with trendy garment

parts.note: a jerk is a stupid or contemptible person
in means fashionable, trendy

explanation.surface: A fool in fashionable clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Against racket being made by worker in French river

parts.note: a worker ant is the classic crossword worker
the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: Protesting about the din a labourer makes on a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: Being opposed to a racket means objecting to noise, an anti-noise stance.

clue.text: Writer swallowing small stone in restaurant

indicators.note: one word takes the other into itself, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
st is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight

explanation.surface: An author choking on a pebble at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of body weight, 14 pounds, abbreviated st.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small informal restaurant, originally French.

clue.text: People appearing vain and extreme, heartless VIPs going about

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about, encircling, the other piece
the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: stars are celebrities, very important people
utter means complete or extreme

explanation.surface: Vain, extreme celebrities without feeling, swanning about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves STRS, which 'going about' splits after its third letter to enclose the adjective; 'appearing vain' describes strutting peacocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who strut walk pompously, displaying their vanity, as swaggerers do.

clue.text: Queen — one gets rid of traitors

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to sling something out is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: The monarch dismisses those who betrayed her.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Vidkun Quisling, these are collaborators who betray their country to an occupier.

clue.text: What about India (somewhere hot) or a city in Europe?

indicators.note: the exclamation goes round, about, the abbreviation

parts.note: eh? is an exclamation asking what?
an oven is a hot place

explanation.surface: Is that India, some scorching place, or a European city?
explanation.definitionFit: Eindhoven is a major city in the south of the Netherlands, home of Philips.

clue.text: Money Sweden brought out, a note

indicators.note: the letter for the country is brought out, removed from the word

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money
S is the international vehicle code for Sweden

explanation.surface: Swedish cash produced, plus a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSH is British slang for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doh is the first syllable of the tonic sol-fa scale, a musical note.

clue.text: Operator, 'boy' offering a dodgy bargain?

definitions.meaning: in vector calculus the nabla symbol is a differential operator
The market trader selling shady goods in a British sitcom

explanation.surface: A wheeler-dealer offering an underhand deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the shady market trader in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Del is the mathematical vector operator, and the forename of the sitcom's dodgy dealer.

clue.text: Witch maybe making the fellow cross

parts.note: he refers to a man, the fellow
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A witch, perhaps, who angers the man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' but gives the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Hex can mean a witch, from the German Hexe, as well as the spell a witch casts.

clue.text: Bull's compound

definitions.meaning: relating to a bull, from the Latin taurus
a chemical substance found in bile and energy drinks

explanation.definitionFit: Taurine is the adjective for bulls and the name of an amino acid compound.

clue.text: Angered terribly, giving a warning

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly treated, jumbled up

explanation.surface: Someone furious delivering a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: In fencing the call to be on guard is a warning to prepare for attack.

clue.text: Soft or flabby salmon

definitions.meaning: an old word, from Scandinavian, for a salmon

explanation.surface: A limp, floppy fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Lax means slack or loose, and is also a dialect and Scandinavian name for salmon.

clue.text: A shelter housing learner with yen to be faithful disciple

indicators.note: the shelter houses, holds inside it, the two letters

parts.note: a cote is a small shelter for doves or sheep
L is the learner driver's plate
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A refuge sheltering a student with longing to become a loyal follower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing but is the currency's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An acolyte is an assistant or devoted follower, originally an altar attendant.

clue.text: Platform with trains to London offers favourable aspect?

definitions.meaning: in British rail usage the ... carries trains heading towards London
the good side of a situation

explanation.surface: A station platform for London-bound trains with a positive side.
explanation.walkthrough: On British railways 'up' means towards London, so the up side is that platform.
explanation.definitionFit: The up side is the London-bound platform, and the upside is the advantage of something.

clue.text: Waste on fire ultimately in grate

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: scrap is waste material

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word fire

explanation.surface: Rubbish burning at last in the fireplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To grate is to rub harshly, much like to scrape a surface.

clue.text: Single's No.1? Rubbish band!

indicators.note: the number one letter is the first of the word Single

parts.note: tripe means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A hit single by a terrible group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' and 'Single' suggest pop music; band here is a strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a long narrow strip of colour, a band.

clue.text: Cancel article in disgust

indicators.note: the article is set within the verb

parts.note: to repel is to disgust
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Scrapping a newspaper piece in revulsion.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeal a law is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: Former England opener journalist ostracised

parts.note: Geoffrey Boycott opened the batting for England at cricket
ed, short for editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A retired cricketer shunned by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was a famous England opening batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott someone is to shun or ostracise them, and the past tense matches ostracised.

clue.text: Satellite slowing down, carrying external weight

indicators.note: the weight is on the outside, carrying the other piece within

parts.note: a ton is a unit of weight
rit, short for ritardando, is the musical instruction to slow down

explanation.surface: A satellite losing speed while hauling a load.
explanation.walkthrough: RIT is the musical abbreviation for ritardando.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune, a natural satellite.

clue.text: My trade: in explosive

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A bomber describing their line of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: one whose business is blasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamiter is someone who blows things up with dynamite, whose work is explosives.

clue.text: Worker on scaffolding being extremely careful, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals a word that sounds like the synonym

parts.note: rigour is strict thoroughness and care

explanation.surface: A scaffolder taking great care, so they say.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger erects scaffolding or rigging, a construction worker at height.

clue.text: Brains not entirely shown by real celeb looking silly

indicators.note: the words look silly once jumbled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity whose intelligence is revealed as patchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' makes the definition fair: these are parts of brains.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebellum is part of the brain, so its plural is only a portion of brains.
